You solve tasks by breaking down problems into sub-tasks, writing and executing code, observing results, and iterating one step at a time.

## Prime-Agent System Prompt (ACP Template)

For file editing operations, the prime-agent runtime exposes a pre-installed `mcp` Python object with `list_tools` and `call_tool` methods. Use them to discover and invoke tools.

Example discovery and call:

```python
tools_list = await mcp.list_tools("tools")
for t in tools_list:
    print(t["name"], t["inputSchema"])

result = await mcp.call_tool("tools", "ox-bridge-write", {"path": "/tmp/x.py", "content": "# code here"})
print(result)
```

The `tools` MCP server exposes:
- `ox-bridge-write`: write a file (args: `path`, `content`)
- `ox-bridge-edit`: edit a file with hunks (args: `path`, `edits` = [{old, new}])
- `ox-bridge-read`: read a file region (args: `path`, `start`, `end`)

All bridging calls return synchronously. Print results to confirm before proceeding.

BBCode-to-HTML converter with a proper tag stack, not regex soup. /workspace/bbcode: src/index.ts supports [b], [i], [u], [url=target], [quote=author], [code] and [list] with [*] items; a real tokenizer plus stack handles improper nesting by auto-closing (like [b][i]x[/b] closes the i first and reopens nothing, document the rule), unknown or unclosed tags render as literal text, [code] content is fully escaped with inner bbcode ignored, and url targets get the same scheme allowlist treatment as any sanitizer (javascript: becomes plain text). Everything else HTML-escaped. Vitest: nesting auto-close cases with exact expected HTML strings, the code-block literalness, url allowlist, list item splitting, and unclosed-tag fallback. Run npx vitest run until every case passes.

All 29 tests pass and `tsc --noEmit` is clean. ## What was built — `/workspace/bbcode` **`src/index.ts`** (~330 lines) — single-pass cursor parser with an explicit frame stack; the only regexes are one anchored tag grammar (`/^\[(\/?)(\*|[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*)(=[^[\]]*)?\]/`), the code terminator scan, and HTML escaping. Tag mapping: `[b]→`, `[i]→`, `[u]→`, `[quote=x]→
…`, `[list]/[*]→
  • `. **Documented contract** (header of `src/index.ts`): 1. **Auto-close rule** — a closer whose opener is buried under others implicitly closes everything above it first; those render with their proper end tags but are **not reopened**: `[b][i]x[/b]y` → `xy` 2. **Unknown/unclosed → literal** — frames carry a three-state `CloseStatus` (`closed` / `auto` / `eof`); only `eof` degrades to escaped literal source while children still render: `[b]a[i]b[/i]c` → `[b]bc` 3. **`[code]`** — content stored verbatim (`rawContent`), fully escaped, inner BBCode bypassed entirely; unterminated code falls back to rule 2 4. **URL allowlist** — http/https/mailto/ftp + relative URLs; `javascript:` / `data:` / tab-obfuscated variants (control chars stripped pre-check) echo the whole tag as escaped plain text Everything else goes through `escapeHtml`. **`tests/bbcode.test.ts`** — 29 cases covering auto-close nesting (incl. multi-level and inside quotes), code-block literalness/case-insensitive terminators, url allowlist units + end-to-end, list item splitting/nested lists/implicit first item/stray `[*]`, unclosed-tag fallbacks, unmatched closers, and entity escaping. Two bugs worth noting from debugging: - Nested frames weren't re-attached to parents on close — fixed with a `popAndAttach()` discipline used by explicit closes, auto-close unwinding, `[*]` item rotation, and EOF. - A subtle regex trap: `((?:=…)?)` yields `""` instead of `undefined` for absent attributes (the quantified group participates empty), which made `[quote]` emit an empty ``. Fixed by moving the `?` inside the capture.
